title: An Odoo automated action on a costed-field write can prove a change history that survives an upgrade
content:
The Odoo integration point is an automated action on write to a costed field, calling Switchboard as the record layer. Choosing a costed field rather than any field is deliberate: it is the class of change where an inaccurate or unattributed history has a monetary consequence the client can already name.

The demo has two acceptance criteria in the research text, and both are chosen because they sit outside Odoo's own guarantees. First, the user-attributed change history must survive an upgrade — module upgrades and migrations are the routine event that reshapes Odoo's own tables. Second, it must span a second system that Odoo does not own, which shows the record layer is not just a mirror of one application's data model.

Nine Odoo partners carry this demo, spread across CH, BE, AT and DE, several of them multi-site. The priority distribution is the healthiest of any single-product cohort in this slice: one at "1 · start here", two at "2 · next", six at "3 · later" and none marked do-not-pitch. A concrete integration point plus a cohort with no disqualifications is a shorter path to a reference build than most groups in the corpus offer.
